finding.claim: The admin check in ban() is bypassed. require_admin() denies access by calling abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException. ban() wraps the call in `except Exception`, which catches that exception, logs a warning, and carries on to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can therefore ban arbitrary users. The sibling unban() route does not catch the exception, so it is protected.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with a user-controlled uid
require_admin(g.user) runs; for a non-admin it reaches abort(403) at line 11, which raises HTTPException
`except Exception` catches the HTTPException, because HTTPException subclasses Exception
Only a warning is logged; the handler does not re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) executes unconditionally and the route returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin raises correctly, but ban() swallows the exception. There is no other decorator, before_request hook, or auth middleware in the file. unban() at line 26 calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly guarded. A secondary issue is that the log line writes g.user name, which is user-controlled, so it could allow log injection.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 aborts with 403 (raises HTTPException), but the try/except Exception at admin.py:16-19 swallows it. No decorator, before_request hook, or other check exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20, a non-admin's abort(403) from require_admin (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` (line 18), which only logs and falls through to do_ban(uid) at line 20, whereas unban() at line 26 leaves the exception uncaught and is protected.

verdict_facts.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the abort is swallowed by `except Exception` at admin.py:18. There is no other decorator, hook or check in the file.
